answer: AI-agent economies running tasks like surveying timber on a meadow ridge can deter Sybil attacks via memory-hard Cuckoo Cycle admission. Each epoch, an agent seeds a bipartite graph from its public key and a beacon hash, returning a small cycle witness that peers verify in milliseconds. This imposes real DRAM bandwidth and energy costs per active identity rather than free cloning. Still, well-funded attackers can rent burst cloud GPUs to solve puzzles in parallel.
